[[File:FuneralPyre.png|thumb|right|250px|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] gave his father a Jedi funeral on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].]]
{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>''Bard'ika'', it's cremation for a Jedi Knight, yes?''"<br />"''It is, ''Kal'buir."<br />"''Tomorrow, then—a final night in her own home with her family around her, and then she goes to the Force, or the ''manda'', or wherever, like the Jedi she was.|[[Kal Skirata]] and [[Bardan Jusik]], planning the funeral of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Etain Tur-Mukan]]|<ref name="Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>}}
'''Jedi funerals''' occurred when a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] had [[Death/Legends|died]] and was [[Cremation/Legends|cremated]]. Exceptions to this [[Funeral/Legends|funeral]] practice were made in times of war, when a body was left in an extreme environment, or in very rare cases when the Jedi used a [[Force ghost/Legends|technique]] to retain their identity after death, and therefore, physically disappear upon their death. The case of [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] was different, his body did not disappear, but he still appeared to [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] numerous times in the following years.

The [[Imperial Knight]]s also adopted this ceremony as their own, as evidenced by the last rites of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Roan Fel]].
